question.question:
Net income 227000 USD includes depreciation 30000 USD, the sale gain, interest expense and dividend income 16500 USD. Equipment costing 91000 USD, 60% depreciated, was sold for 55500 USD cash. A 550000 USD loan was outstanding all year; interest expense is 8% of it. Interest payable was 2 months of interest at year start and 1 months at year end; interest paid is expense minus the payable increase. Net operating working capital changed by -20000 USD (a positive increase reduces operating cash). Policy: interest paid is financing, so operating adds back the full expense and ignores the payable change; dividends received (all in cash) are investing, so operating removes dividend income; the gain (negative if a loss) is subtracted in operating and full proceeds are investing. Compute operating cash flow.

Answer format: return only the exact numeric value interpreted in `usd`, using finite-decimal notation when it terminates in base 10 and an irreducible `numerator/denominator` fraction otherwise, with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: Signed gain on the equipment sale, negative if a loss
Interest expense accrued on the loan for the year
Interest paid in cash, reported as a financing outflow magnitude
Net investing cash flow including sale proceeds and dividends received
